32_marg1501: All wisdom, etc. Jerome says that he found the book of Jesus the son of Sirach among the Hebrews, entitled not Ecclesiasticus, as among the Latins, but Parables; and with it were joined Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs, so that it matched Solomon not only in the number of books but in the kind of their matter. But the book of Wisdom he did not find among them; rather it smacks of Greek eloquence, and some affirm that it is Philo’s. Ecclesiasticus, like Ecclesiastes, is most useful to the Church; the name means one who gathers or collects, as the other means a preacher. But Ecclesiastes is referred to Christ, Ecclesiasticus to any preacher, who for the excellence of his virtues is called Panaretos, that is, capable of all the virtues. Its clearness and its Latinity are so great that it is its own commentary.
32_marg1502: All wisdom, etc. Rabanus. He begins from the eternal wisdom of God, which is Christ, who is always with the Father before the ages, according to that: “In the beginning was the Word: and the Word was with God,” etc.

Of the other it is written: “The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever.” For each one fears lest he lose good things and the presence of God, which he desires to enjoy for ever; of which it is said: The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart.
